profile.what: India's largest IT services company: application development and maintenance, enterprise solutions (SAP, Salesforce, Oracle), cloud and infrastructure services, cybersecurity, engineering, business process services and software products (TCS BaNCS, ignio, iON), sold to large enterprises in North America (48%), the UK (17%), continental Europe (15%) and elsewhere.
profile.owner: Tata Sons Pvt Ltd holds 71.74% (2,59,54,99,419 shares) of 3,61,80,87,518 shares (AR FY26 note 8(m)); total promoter group 71.77% at Jun-2026 (Trendlyne compilation of the exchange filing).

shares.note: Weighted average shares FY26 = 3,61,80,87,518 (AR FY26 P&L). Screener's FY26 Net Profit (Rs49,454 cr, incl. Rs244 cr minorities) / EPS (136.01) implies 363.6 cr, 0.5% above the real count; below the 1% threshold, so no patch: forecast PAT incl. minorities / 363.6 cr gives attributable EPS to within 0.1%.

reporting.segments: TCS reports eight industry verticals (BFSI; Consumer Business; Life Sciences & Healthcare; Manufacturing; Technology & Services; Communication & Media; Energy, Resources & Utilities; Regional Markets & Others) and seven geographies, with constant-currency (CC) growth. The vertical scheme changed in FY23 (Retail & CPG became Consumer Business; ERU split out of Regional Markets), so FY21-22 verticals are not comparable.
reporting.margins: TCS reports operating margin = operating income after depreciation, before other income, as % of revenue (an EBIT margin). Finance costs sit in 'other income (expense), net' in its IFRS/fact-sheet P&L. Screener's 'Operating Profit' = TCS operating income + depreciation (FY26: 66,838 + 5,560 = 72,398), so the engine's EBITDA margin = TCS EBIT margin + depreciation/revenue.
reporting.costReclass: From Q1FY27 TCS refined cost categories (no impact on totals or margins) and stopped splitting cost of revenue and SG&A in the fact sheet (callQ1FY27, CFO).
reporting.attrition: LTM attrition in IT services; from Q2FY26 TCS reports voluntary LTM attrition (definition change).

fy26.note: AR FY26 P&L and notes 20, 25, 26: restructuring (Jul-2025 programme to release associates whose deployment was not feasible; Rs1,135 cr in Q2FY26 and Rs253 cr in Q3FY26), statutory impact of the four Labour Codes notified 21-Nov-2025 (Q3FY26), and US$112 m for the CSC/DXC trade-secret judgement (Q3FY26) plus US$38 m of interest in finance costs. Screener nets the Rs4,526 cr of exceptional items into other income (4,402 - 4,526 = -124). EPS 136.01 reported vs 145.99 before one-offs.

q1fy27.marginBridge: Wage increments -170 bp; partnership ecosystem and targeted investments; partly offset by +40 bp currency and operational efficiencies (CFO).
q1fy27.megaDeal: SKF: US$800 m+ net-new AI-led transformation (infrastructure, applications, S/4HANA, business processes); five-year tenure per JM Financial's management meeting (BT, 8-Sep-2026). Sixth mega deal in five quarters.

callPoints: Demand: clients deferred some projects as geopolitical uncertainty rose from March; CEO expects demand to improve 'sometime in Q2' on pent-up technology backlog (callQ1FY27).

Verticals: BFSI good across geographies; Technology growing; Consumer Business hit by inflation and geopolitics (North American airlines, non-essential retail) and large projects ending; Life Sciences declined, recovery 'expected soon'; Manufacturing soft in auto but net-new wins (SKF, ABB); CMI modest; ERU slight decline (callQ1FY27).

AI deflation: 'in most places, the productivity gain passed on is around 10% to 15%' as contracts renew, usually compensated by additional work; TCS does not see a 'massive contraction' (CEO, callQ1FY27).
AI revenue is lumpy (12-16 week projects, little annuity); +US$75 m annualised in Q1 vs +US$125 m in Q4 (callQ1FY27).
Margins: 'exit at 25% plus' in FY27; aspiration to 'progressively inch up closer, at least to the FY26 levels'; longer term 'move towards 26%' (CFO, callQ1FY27 and callQ4FY26).
Hiring: +9,279 net in Q1; CEO disagrees that AI will drastically cut white-collar employment; 14,000 campus graduates onboarded in Q4FY26 (callQ1FY27).
Partnerships: Anthropic (50,000 Claude licences, dedicated business unit), Mistral (first GSI partner), ServiceNow, Google Cloud; SovereignSecure Cloud for Europe; GCC business unit (prQ1FY27).

guidance.said: 'Confident of a good CY2026' on client conversations and deal momentum (CEO).
guidance.outcome: Q4FY26 CC +1.2% QoQ, Q1FY27 +0.4%: growth, but slow

guidance.said: Rs2,128 cr provision; ongoing impact ~10-15 bp of margin, no further one-offs expected unless the rules change.
Restructuring programme 'completed'; no one-offs in Q4.
guidance.outcome: Q1FY27 one-off was legal (CSC), not restructuring

guidance.said: 'Quite positive' on FY27 and international growth; expects a stronger 1H; no number given.
Increments for all grades from 1-Apr-2026; impact similar to past cycles, 150-200 bp.
Exiting FY26 at a four-year-high 25%; 'would like to move towards 26%, but on a longer-term basis'.
Initial aim is to 'arrest the degrowth while the AI revenue increase'; AI revenue productivity 'much better' than average.
guidance.outcome: AI run-rate US$2.6 bn (Q1FY27), ~8.5% of revenue

guidance.said: Take the wage hit upfront in Q1, inch up through the year; 'exit at 25% plus'.

guidance.item: Q2 and medium term (via JM Financial)
guidance.said: Q2 'better than' Q1; FY27 better than FY26; high-single-digit growth could return once productivity-led deflation is absorbed; BSNL final order awaited, ramp over 6-9 months, smaller than the last; buyback remains an option.

hyperVault.what: AI data-centre subsidiary (HyperVault AI Data Center Ltd, incorporated 29-Oct-2025) to build >1 GW of AI-ready capacity over 'the next few years'; TCS builds the shell, power and cooling; clients bring compute.
hyperVault.funding: TCS and TPG to invest up to Rs18,000 cr in the ratio 51:49 (agreements 20-Nov-2025); TPG subscribed 49% (Rs199.4 cr first tranche) on 9-Mar-2026, so HyperVault is a 51% subsidiary (consolidated, with a minority interest). Original plan (Oct-2025): >US$6.5 bn for 1 GW over 5-7 years, equity plus debt, revenue from 18-24 months.
hyperVault.customers: OpenAI: 100 MW committed with an option to 1 GW (Feb-2026); AMD Helios rack-scale blueprint up to 200 MW (Feb-2026).
hyperVault.sites: Pune (88 acres, Rs640.5 cr) and Anakapalli (~200 acres) land (Jul-2026); Hyderabad 264-acre campus of up to 1 GW where HyperVault 'and its partners' will invest up to Rs70,000 cr (exchange filing, ~5-Sep-2026).
hyperVault.ourTreatment: We model TCS's 51% equity share of the Rs18,000 cr programme (~Rs9,200 cr) as extra capex of ~Rs3,000 cr a year in FY27-29E and no HyperVault revenue (first revenue not before FY28; size unknown).

bsnl.what: Advance purchase order of >Rs15,000 cr (22-May-2023) for a TCS-led consortium (with Tejas Networks and C-DoT) to roll out BSNL's indigenous 4G network; add-on APO of Rs2,903 cr for 18,685 more sites (21-May-2025).
bsnl.effect: Lifted India revenue to 8.6% of FY25 revenue (India CC +62.6% in FY25), then tapered from Q1FY26 (India -31.4% QoQ in Q1FY26, 2.6 pp of TCS's -3.3% QoQ CC); India -28.6% CC in FY26. Equipment purchased from Tejas (a Tata Sons subsidiary) explains related-party purchases of Rs8,178 cr in FY25 vs Rs1,002 cr in FY26 and 'cost of equipment and software licences' of Rs11,648 cr vs Rs4,399 cr.
bsnl.next: Final purchase order for the add-on awaited (Sep-2026); some revenue could start in Q2FY27 with a 6-9 month ramp; Tejas announced a Rs1,537 cr TCS order for the 18,685 sites (28-Aug-2026).
